text:
carla (sec): heads up — partner ingestion pipeline logs leaked a wrapped blob that looks like a KMS-wrapped secret. spotted in partner-logs-archive around 03:12 UTC. i redacted the blob in the archive but we need containment + quick rotation.

dinesh: confirmed, i pulled the object. it contains a base64 blob with a GCP KMS ciphertext header. not a plaintext credential but we should assume potential exposure and rotate.

leo (infra): quick checklist: 1) revoke any active SA keys that had access to that bucket 2) disable the KMS key's CryptoKeyVersions for signing/unwrap 3) kick off vault transit rewrap for any values using that key.

carla (sec): +1. also we need to tighten RBAC on partner ingestion role — it was overly broad. who owns the partner role?

security-oncall: tagging @leo and @dinesh. i'll take ownership of the incident timeline. proposed immediate actions (T0..): T0: snapshot logs + remove archived blob from public bucket; T+10m: rotate KMS key; T+20m: rotate affected vault transit keys and re-encrypt secrets; T+30m: revoke any exposed SA keys; T+1h: audit logs export and run regression evals on services.

dinesh: for KMS rotate -> we should create a new CryptoKey ring key version, set it as primary, and then rewrap ciphertexts. note: GCP automatic rewrap will not happen; we need explicit re-encrypt in Vault or our rewrap job.

leo (infra): i'm already spinning up a canary rewrap job in k8s-job-runner; will target low-traffic namespace first. config: `gcloud kms keys versions create --key=ingest-key --keyring=partner-keys --location=global` then set `gcloud kms keys set-primary` on new version. also adding a temporary deny binding for `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` for partner SA.

carla (sec): RBAC change: reduce partner-internal role to read-only for bucket, remove list/get on project-level secrets. we need an acl change that expires in 24h until we finish root-cause.

security-oncall: logged tasks in the incident tracker: 8943219876-1 revoke-sa-keys, 8943219876-2 create-kms-version, 8943219876-3 rewrap-vault-values, 8943219876-4 audit-export. assigning owners. please ack when done.

rotations-bot: scheduled job `rewrap-job-8943219876` created, run strategy=canary batch_size=5 namespaces=[platform,auth] retry=3 ETA 03:40 UTC.

dinesh: note — we have to rotate any long-lived Vault-to-GCS service tokens. i'll add a script to identify tokens with `path: kv/partner/*` and create new versions. also recommend creating a migration window and short TTL for new tokens.

leo (infra): audit logging: enabling object-level ACL audit (Data Access logs) on the partner bucket and forwarding to secure BigQuery dataset `redwood_incident_audit`. will include IAM change diffs.

carla (sec): vuln triage note: seems likely root cause was partner CI accidentally uploading diagnostic bundle that included wrapped ciphertexts. need to follow up with partner eng to change their upload workflow.

security-oncall: quick status check — revoke-sa-keys done (dinesh), kms new version created (leo), rewrap canary started (leo), RBAC tightened (carla). next: full rewrap sweep and TTL enforcement.

dinesh: canary results look good, no app errors for auth-service. planning full sweep now, ETA 40m.

carla (sec): great. after sweep, we'll rotate Vault master transit key and update our KMS binding to use a new key ring policy with least-priv. also file a compliance ticket for SOC2 evidence.

security-oncall: final note — preserve original archived blob in an evidence bucket with restricted access (audit-only) and record chain of custody. tagging this thread for postmortem writeup. :white_check_mark:

leo (infra): ack. will also add a temporary alert: high rate of kms.decrypt errors -> page sec-oncall.

carla (sec): thanks everyone — update incidents/8943219876 when you finish tasks. we'll do a short retro tomorrow 15:00 UTC.

security-oncall: incident closed for immediate containment; follow-ups scheduled.
